229.text: "The economic support offered to the blockaders was well received."
229.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Floating_GolcondistProtestsTwo_ForceBreak"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Floating_DastnuristProtestsTwo_CapitalPolice"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Floating_GolcondistProtestsTwo_NegotiateSettlement"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Floating_GolcondistProtestsTwo_FinancialIncentive"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Floating_GolcondistProtestsOne_GoldenGuardSent"] == false)

233.speaker: Sal Ignacius

244.text: "The blockade has ended, and the city is returning to normal."

245.speaker: Sal Ignacius
245.text: "Local commerce is resuming, and the goodwill towards the Crown is notable."

249.speaker: Player_Romus
249.text: "One day it’s reverence, the next it’s unrest. The faithful are never still for long."

250.speaker: Player_Romus
250.text: "Comforting, isn’t it? To know we rule a kingdom of such pious malcontents."

252.speaker: Player_Romus
252.text: "So much of the realm turns on belief. We cannot afford to misstep with any of them."

260.speaker: Player_Romus
260.text: "That’s heartening news. Perhaps the tide is turning in our favor."

272.speaker: Narrator
272.text: He gave a small nod of respect.

273.speaker: Sal Ignacius
273.text: "There’s no denying it, Your Majesty. The decision to make the kingdom a secular state has shaken Rizia to its core."

274.speaker: Sal Ignacius
274.text: "Our Wruhecist congregants, Golcondists among them, see your decree as a retreat from the divine order."

281.speaker: Sal Ignacius
281.text: “There’s no denying, Your Majesty, the decision to make Nurity the foundation of the state has stirred deep emotions."

282.speaker: Sal Ignacius
282.text: "While Dastnurists have embraced the new order, the Wruhecist community feels their faith has been sidelined."

283.speaker: Player_Romus
283.text: "So now protecting a sanctuary is controversial? I didn't realize law and order need approval ratings."

285.speaker: Player_Romus
285.text: "I didn’t take the decision lightly. I stand by it."

286.speaker: Player_Romus
286.text: "Some things are sacred. That was one of them."

290.speaker: Player_Romus
290.text: "Let them talk. By next week, they'll forget all about it."

291.speaker: Player_Romus
291.text: “Tradition holds the spine of this kingdom together. They’d do well to remember that.”

292.speaker: Player_Romus
292.text: “As they should. Unity with the Crown is no small matter.”

293.speaker: Player_Romus
293.text: “Let the cities take note. The soil breeds loyalty."

299.speaker: Player_Romus
299.text: “God sees sacrifice. So does the Crown.”

300.speaker: Player_Romus
300.text: “Then the old guard still has teeth. Good.”

301.speaker: Player_Romus
301.text: "Dissenters will grow into their complaints. Or grow out of them.”

303.speaker: Player_Romus
303.text: “Burning lies was the easy part. Convincing them they’re lies is harder.”

304.speaker: Player_Romus
304.text: “One man’s heresy is another man’s future.”

305.speaker: Player_Romus
305.text: “They wanted a compromise. This is what it looks like.”

306.speaker: Player_Romus
306.text: “They may see it as lenient, but I see it as principled. We upheld the law without silencing dissent.”

307.speaker: Player_Romus
307.text: “Faith has its place. So does order.”

308.speaker: Player_Romus
308.text: "That’s not the message I intended to send."

309.speaker: Player_Romus
309.text: "If they wanted restraint, they should’ve shown it first."

310.speaker: Player_Romus
310.text: "I defend the realm. Let the Sanctuary defend the faith."

311.speaker: Player_Romus
311.text: "If ink threatens them, perhaps their faith is thinner than they claim."

312.speaker: Player_Romus
312.text: "Good. Let them gather. The more they speak in my name, the less room there is for dissent."

316.speaker: Player_Romus
316.text: "And here I thought all I did was permit a prayer circle."

317.speaker: Player_Romus
317.text: "That was the intention. I trust they remember who allowed it."

321.speaker: Player_Romus
321.text: "Nothing moves the spirit quite like a call to arms."

322.speaker: Player_Romus
322.text: "Good. They’ll defend the Kingdom as fiercely as they defend their faith."

323.speaker: Player_Romus
323.text: "Let it be said the Crown inspires more than sermons ever could."

327.speaker: Player_Romus
327.text: "I respect their sacrifice. May it be returned to them tenfold in peace."

328.speaker: Player_Romus
328.text: "A little discomfort in the name of unity. I think they’ll survive."

329.speaker: Player_Romus
329.text: "The price of faith is rarely measured in guilders. But guilders certainly help."

333.speaker: Player_Romus
333.text: "Let the young grumble. They’ll inherit tradition, not rewrite it."

334.speaker: Player_Romus
334.text: "The old guard remembers why the Crown still stands. I’ll take their trust."

335.speaker: Player_Romus
335.text: "They’ll thank me in ten years. Or curse me. Either way, they’ll remember."

339.speaker: Sal Ignacius
339.text: "When the call is just, the faithful will answer."

340.speaker: Sal Ignacius
340.text: "Their hearts belong to both. You’ve given them reason."

341.speaker: Sal Ignacius
341.text: "Some would call that pride, not inspiration."

344.speaker: Sal Ignacius
344.text: "To them, it was far more than that."

346.speaker: Sal Ignacius
346.text: "Inheritance is a powerful teacher, Your Majesty."

347.speaker: Sal Ignacius
347.text: "They have long memories, and steady hearts."

348.speaker: Sal Ignacius
348.text: "It’s legacy that endures, even if gratitude doesn’t."

349.speaker: Player_Romus
349.text: "That’s not the image I intended to leave behind. We need to tread more carefully."

350.speaker: Player_Romus
350.text: "They were blocking roads, not kneeling in prayer."

352.speaker: Player_Romus
352.text: "Good. I prefer open gates to raised voices."

354.speaker: Player_Romus
354.text: "Let them be pleased. We didn’t concede, we governed."

355.speaker: Player_Romus
355.text: "If goodwill is the outcome, then the price was fair."

356.speaker: Player_Romus
356.text: "So it turns out their convictions had a price tag after all."

357.speaker: Player_Romus
357.text: "I would’ve preferred loyalty. But contentment will suffice."

358.speaker: Player_Romus
358.text: "I hate that it came to that. But inaction would’ve been far worse."

360.speaker: Player_Romus
360.text: "Strength alienates the weak. I can live with that."

361.speaker: Player_Romus
361.text: "It wasn’t fair. But I needed something to defuse the moment."

362.speaker: Player_Romus
362.text: "It ended. I’m less concerned with how it played."

363.speaker: Player_Romus
363.text: "Well, I couldn’t very well blame the weather."

364.speaker: Sal Ignacius
364.text: "Then we’ll walk with more care, Your Majesty."

365.speaker: Sal Ignacius
365.text: "Perhaps. But to them, the act felt sacred."

368.speaker: Sal Ignacius
368.text: "They are also more enduring when given in good faith."

369.speaker: Sal Ignacius
369.text: "If that’s true, Majesty, then you’ve governed well."

370.speaker: Sal Ignacius
370.text: "Few rulers count peace as profit. I’m glad you do."

371.speaker: Sal Ignacius
371.text: "Or perhaps they simply chose peace over pride."

372.speaker: Sal Ignacius
372.text: "Sometimes contentment grows into loyalty, if nurtured."

375.speaker: Sal Ignacius
375.text: "Even the weak were made by His hand, Majesty. They, too, are under your charge."

376.speaker: Sal Ignacius
376.text: "I understand why. But we must be careful not to trade trust for convenience."

377.speaker: Sal Ignacius
377.text: "But they are, Your Majesty. And their memory is long."

378.speaker: Sal Ignacius
378.text: "Maybe. But unjust blame can linger like floodwaters."

382.speaker: Sal Ignacius
382.text: “And the recent lifting of our homosexuality ban has only deepened the sense of moral decline."

387.speaker: Sal Ignacius
387.text: "Combined with your decriminalization of homosexuality, I fear a sense of moral decay is sinking in."

388.speaker: Sal Ignacius
388.text: "But the recent decriminalization of homosexuality has tested my congregants' long-standing beliefs."

392.speaker: Sal Ignacius
392.text: "Overall, their view of you is neither favorable nor unfavorable."

393.speaker: Player_Romus
393.text: "Then I’ve mastered the art of being tolerable."

400.speaker: Player_Romus
400.text: "The faithful are easily unsettled by change, especially when it touches what they hold most sacred."

401.speaker: Sal Ignacius
401.text: "So it has always been, Your Majesty."

402.speaker: Player_Romus
402.text: "That decree is not up for debate. I made my decision and I stand by it."

403.speaker: Player_Romus
403.text: "They act as if Nurity were foreign to them... I intended to increase faith in Rizia, not curtail it."

404.speaker: Sal Ignacius
404.text: "Perhaps, Your Majesty, but unity imposed can feel like loss to those who weren’t ready to receive it."

405.speaker: Player_Romus
405.text: "I gave our people religious freedom. If they're offended, their faith was never that deep."

406.speaker: Sal Ignacius
406.text: "With all due respect, Your Majesty, I did voice this concern to you earlier."

410.speaker: Sal Ignacius
410.text: "If you had consulted with me on this beforehand, I would have warned you against it."

414.speaker: Player_Romus
414.text: "I bet the Golcondists don't feel that way."

415.speaker: Sal Ignacius
415.text: "Indeed, they welcomed the change. But their jubilation has made the rest of the kingdom all the more furious."

416.speaker: Sal Ignacius
416.text: "I understand, Your Majesty, but you must have known that a backlash was inevitable."

417.speaker: Player_Romus
417.text: "Our strict adherence to Wruhecism was creating unnecessary division. Now the kingdom has been unified."

418.speaker: Sal Ignacius
418.text: "I am afraid Wruhecists do not see it that way."

446.text: "To the point that they have begun to align with the reformist movement."

463.speaker: Sal Ignacius
463.text: "Thankfully, only Golcondists thus far, Though with their militant tendencies, they could contribute to the chaos significantly."

464.speaker: Player_Romus
464.text: "That's not good news. I've got to find a way to win back the support of the faithful."

465.speaker: Player_Romus
465.text: "These congregants you're speaking of... can they be swayed from the reformists' side?"

469.speaker: Player_Romus
469.text: "The leader of the reformists is a godless Malenyevist. Do they really think he'll respect their religion more than I do?"

470.speaker: Sal Ignacius
470.text: "Yet with enough encouragement from the Crown, they will return to the monarchy's side."

471.speaker: Player_Romus
471.text: "The whole country hungers for change, it seems. Even those who've been mired in tradition for so long."

473.speaker: Sal Ignacius
473.text: "I believe they can. But only if the Crown addresses their concerns."

474.speaker: Sal Ignacius
474.text: "He claims he will give them a voice. Something I very much doubt."

475.speaker: Sal Ignacius
475.text: "Agreed. If we foster peace among religious groups, they could become a powerful advocate of the Crown."

479.speaker: Player_Romus
479.text: "In times of unrest, it is good to know the faithful are on my side."

483.speaker: Narrator
483.text: A mysterious expression passed across Sal's face.

486.speaker: Player_Romus
486.text: "What? How could they choose Manus Sazon over me?"
